01.r: Give back to the poor what the lenders have taken.
01.n: The causative form of the ordinary verb 'to turn back, return': 'make (it) return'. It is plural, addressed to all the lenders.

02.r: Softens the command into an urgent request.
02.n: Gesenius: a particle used in submissive and modest request, often rendered 'now' in English.

04.n: Literally 'as the day', an idiom for 'this very day'. YLT keeps 'as to-day'.

05.r: Farmland handed over to the lenders.

06.r: Vineyards handed over to the lenders.
06.n: Gesenius gives the first sense as a field set with plants of nobler quality, cultivated as a garden or orchard.

07.r: Olive groves handed over to the lenders.
07.n: The word is 'olives' or 'olive trees'; the translations take it as the groves where they grow.

08.r: Houses handed over to the lenders.

s: and the one per cent of
09.r: A hundredth part of the loans, most likely the interest charged on them.
t: and remit the hundreth part of
09.n: The word is 'hundred'; the brief's lexicon lists 'one hundredth' as one of its uses, and BDB gives 'a hundredth part of the money' here. BDB adds that the text may quite possibly be read 'the debt' (a word written much like it). That the hundredth was the rate of interest is a reasonable reading, not something the verse states; the JPS takes it as 'the hundred pieces of silver'.

10.n: Our English keeps 'silver' throughout, as Gesenius gives it first.

11.n: Gesenius: corn. In older English 'corn' meant grain in general.

12.n: Gesenius: must, new wine. The Hebrew has no 'and' before it.

13.n: Gesenius: oil, especially fresh and new, from a root meaning to shine; he notes it is often joined with the word for new wine.

14.r: Introduces what the creditors are claiming.

15.r: The nobles and officials, the creditors.
15.n: The pronoun is written out, which makes it pointed: 'you are the ones'.

16.r: They are claiming these from the poor as creditors.
16.n: A participle of the verb the brief's lexicon gives as to lend, be a creditor; its participle as a noun is the 'creditor' of Exodus 22:25 on this page, so our English renders it 'exact', the creditor's act, and keeps 'lend' for a different verb. Gesenius gives it as to borrow and to lend to someone, the person being marked with the preposition that follows here. Every translation here says 'exact' except the BSB, 'have been assessing'.

17.r: The poor, from whom payment is claimed.
17.n: Literally 'in them' or 'on them'; with this verb the preposition marks the person the claim is made against, so English says 'from'.

_extra.23: καὶ (and): the Greek has no word for the oil; this 'and' leads into its last clause, ἐξενέγκατε ἑαυτοῖς.

01.n: ἐπιστρέφω, to turn back, return. Swete's text numbers this book 2 Esdras.

02.n: δή, a particle that adds urgency, 'now'.

03.n: Printed αὐτοὶ, 'they themselves', in our Greek text; it is likely αὐτοῖς, 'to them', misread.

04.n: ὡς σήμερον, 'as today', exactly the Hebrew idiom.

09.n: The Greek has 'and from', not 'the hundredth': ἀπό, 'from'. A likely explanation is that the translators read the Hebrew letters for 'hundred of' as 'from' (the two are written alike); that is our inference.

12.n: οἶνος, wine. The Greek adds 'and' here.

16.n: Dictionary form supplied; the brief gives none. ἐξενέγκατε, 'carry out, pay out', an imperative. Perhaps the translators read the Hebrew verb as the like-spelled 'carry'; that is our inference.

17.n: Dictionary form corrected: ἑαυτοῖς is from the reflexive ἑαυτοῦ, not αὐτός.
